articles.title: Mill Hill Gets $1,200 for Crosswalk
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in March.
body: The plan calls for crosswalk along Linden Place, with work expected to start in March.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Tuesday mornings.
The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Public works estimates the work will take about 20 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Council Approves $850 for Salem Street Repairs
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Salem Street disagreed about cost and timing.
body: The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Marsh Landing said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Councilmember Lorraine Wojcik asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $850.
Public works estimates the work will take about 9 weeks once it starts in March. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the June meeting. Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

articles.title: Marcus Lacey, 87, Hardware Store Owner
articles.deck: Friends remember Marcus Lacey for the many years of service to Hickory Ridge.
body: Marcus Lacey died in May at home on Ingram Terrace, at the age of 87.

Born in Hickory Ridge in the years after the war, Marcus Lacey spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Hickory Ridge.
